15: 
16: # Codex CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for all Codex CLI commands, flags, models, configuration, and troubleshooting.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Codex CLI is OpenAI's terminal-based AI coding agent powered by `gpt-5.5` — a balanced model used across code generation, review, architecture analysis, and research. The skill dispatches `gpt-5.5` at `medium` reasoning on the `fast` service tier by default; users can override reasoning effort (e.g. "Use gpt 5.5 high fast"). It provides direct access to OpenAI's capabilities from the command line, including code generation, file manipulation, shell execution, web browsing, and multi-turn sessions — all governed by configurable sandbox modes.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29: 
30: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Codex CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, sandbox modes, and troubleshooting guidance.
31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Setting up or configuring Codex CLI
35: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or agent configurations
36: - Troubleshooting authentication, sandbox, or session issues
37: - Configuring agents via `.codex/agents/*.toml`
38: - Selecting the right sandbox mode for a task
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Repository** | https://github.com/openai/codex |
45: | **License** | MIT |
46: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ |
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. INSTALLATION
51: 
52: | Method | Command | Notes |
53: |--------|---------|-------|
54: | **npm global** | `npm i -g @openai/codex` | Persistent install, recommended for scripts |
55: | **Homebrew** | `brew install --cask codex` | macOS-native, auto-updates via `brew upgrade` |
56: | **Upgrade (npm)** | `npm update -g @openai/codex` | Update to latest version |
57: | **Upgrade (Homebrew)** | `brew upgrade --cask codex` | Update via Homebrew |
58: 
59: **Platform support:**
60: 
61: | Platform | Status |
62: |----------|--------|
63: | macOS | Full support |
64: | Linux | Full support |
65: | Windows (WSL) | Experimental — use WSL 2 for best results |
66: 
67: After installation, run `codex` for the full-screen TUI or `codex exec "prompt" --model gpt-5.5` for non-interactive use.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
72: 
73: cli-codex authenticates through **ChatGPT OAuth only** — `codex login` (browser flow). It does not use an OpenAI API key.
74: 
75: **OAuth login/logout:**
76: 
77: ```bash
78: # Authenticate via ChatGPT account (opens browser)
79: codex login
80: 
81: # View authentication status
82: codex login status
83: 
84: # Log out and clear stored credentials
85: codex logout
86: ```
87: 
88: **OAuth account eligibility:** ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, or Enterprise accounts only. Free-tier ChatGPT accounts are not supported.
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 4. COMMAND-LINE FLAGS
93: 
94: ### Essential Flags
95: 
96: | Flag | Short | Values | Description |
97: |------|-------|--------|-------------|
98: | `--model` | `-m` | `gpt-5.5` | Model to use — `gpt-5.5` (default), `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-sol` |
99: | `--config` | `-c` | `key=value` | Override a config.toml value (e.g., `-c model_reasoning_effort="high"`) |
100: | `--sandbox` | `-s` | `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access` | Sandbox mode controlling file/shell access |
101: | `--ask-for-approval` | `-a` | `untrusted`, `on-request`, `never` | Top-level approval policy; place `-a` before `exec` when using the headless form |
102: | `--profile` | `-p` | profile-name | Load a named configuration profile |
103: | `--image` | `-i` | file-path | Attach an image (PNG or JPEG) to the prompt |
104: | `-c approval_policy=never` | | `never` | Headless no-prompt approval policy; `-a never` is the top-level equivalent |
105: | `--oss` | | (none) | Use local open-source models via Ollama instead of OpenAI |
106: | `--search` | | (none) | Enable live web browsing during the session (top-level flag; precede `exec`: `codex --search exec …`) |
107: 
108: ### Profile & Review Flags
109: 
110: | Flag | Description |
111: |------|-------------|
112: | `--profile <name>` / `-p` | Load `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` as a named configuration profile |
113: | `exec review` | Built-in subcommand for git diff-aware code review (supports `--commit`, `--base`, `--uncommitted`) |
114: 
115: ### Approval Mode Values
116: 
117: | Value | Behavior |
118: |-------|----------|
119: | `untrusted` | Prompt for approval on all actions (most cautious) |
120: | `on-request` | Prompt only when the agent marks an action as requiring approval |
121: | `never` | Never prompt; auto-approve all actions |
122: 
123: ### Sandbox Mode Values
124: 
125: | Value | File Access | Shell Commands | Best For |
126: |-------|-------------|----------------|----------|
127: | `read-only` | Read files only | Restricted | Exploration, analysis, review |
128: | `workspace-write` | Read + write workspace files | Controlled | Code generation, documentation |
129: | `danger-full-access` | Full filesystem + shell | Unrestricted | Migration, scripted automation |
130: 
131: ### Config Override Flag (-c)
132: 
133: The `-c` / `--config` flag overrides any `config.toml` value at runtime. Uses dotted paths for nested values. The value is parsed as TOML; if parsing fails, it's used as a literal string.
134: 
135: ```bash
136: # Override reasoning effort
137: codex exec "Analyze this architecture" -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high"
138: 
139: # Override model via -c
140: codex exec "Review code" -c model="gpt-5.5"
141: 
142: # Multiple overrides
143: codex exec "Task" -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c sandbox_mode="read-only"
144: ```
145: 
146: ### Usage Examples
147: 
148: ```bash
149: # Interactive TUI
150: codex
151: 
152: # Non-interactive: exec subcommand
153: codex exec "Refactor utils.ts to use async/await" --model gpt-5.5
154: 
155: # With sandbox mode
156: codex exec "Add error handling to auth.ts" --sandbox workspace-write --model gpt-5.5
157: 
158: # With approval control (top-level flag before exec)
159: codex -a untrusted exec "Clean up deprecated files" --model gpt-5.5
160: 
161: # Headless no-prompt mode
162: codex -a never exec "Run the test suite and fix failures" --model gpt-5.5
163: 
164: # Attach an image
165: codex exec "Implement this UI component" --image wireframe.png --model gpt-5.5
166: 
167: # Enable web search
168: codex --search exec "Research and implement OAuth2 PKCE flow" --model gpt-5.5
169: 
170: # Load a named profile
171: codex exec "Review this PR" --profile review --model gpt-5.5
172: 
173: # Use local OSS model via Ollama
174: codex exec "Refactor this function" --oss
175: ```
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ## 5. MODEL SELECTION
180: 
181: Default: `gpt-5.5` at `-c model_reasoning_effort="medium"` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`). Set reasoning effort with the config override **`-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`** — there is **no `--reasoning-effort` CLI flag** — and keep it within the chosen model's ceiling.
182: 
183: **Full model roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder → [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).**
184: 
185: ### Reasoning Effort Configuration
186: 
187: Reasoning effort controls how much "thinking" the model does. There is **no `--reasoning-effort` CLI flag**. Set it via:
188: 
189: 1. **CLI override:** `-c model_reasoning_effort="high"`
190: 2. **config.toml:** `model_reasoning_effort = "medium"` (global default matching the skill)
191: 3. **Profile:** `$CODEX_HOME/review.config.toml` → `model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"`
192: 4. **Plan mode:** `plan_mode_reasoning_effort = "medium"` (Plan-mode-specific override)
193: 
194: The 8-level effort ladder and its per-model ceilings live in [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md) §4.
195: 
196: ### Selection Strategy
197: 
198: | Task Type | Reasoning Effort | Rationale |
199: |-----------|-----------------|-----------|
200: | Architecture decisions | `high` / `xhigh` | Multi-faceted analysis benefits from deeper thinking |
201: | Security audits | `high` / `xhigh` | Catches subtle vulnerability patterns |
202: | Complex planning | `high` / `xhigh` | Multi-strategy evaluation benefits from depth |
203: | Code generation | `medium` (default) | Balanced for most generation tasks |
204: | Standard code review | `medium` (default) | Efficient for pattern-based review |
205: | Implementation | `medium` (default) | Balanced for translating specs to code |
206: | Test generation | `medium` (default) | Solid for test structure output |
207: | Documentation | `medium` (default) | Efficient for structured doc generation |
208: | Trivial lookups / formatting | `low` / `minimal` | Minimize cost and latency |
209: 
210: Always specify `--model` explicitly in scripts for predictability (`gpt-5.5` is the skill default); omitting it relies on the CLI default, which may change across versions. When a task wants reasoning past `xhigh`, escalate the model — see the roster and ceilings in [providers-and-models.md](./providers-and-models.md).
211: 
212: ### Command-Line Specification
213: 
214: ```bash
215: # Reasoning-heavy tasks — raise reasoning_effort
216: codex exec "Analyze this architecture and identify coupling issues" --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high"
217: codex exec "Security audit of @./src/auth.ts" --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high"
218: 
219: # Code-focused tasks — medium is fine
220: codex exec "Write unit tests for user.ts" --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium"
221: codex exec "Generate a rate limiter middleware" --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium"
222: ```
223: 
224: ### Agent TOML Configuration
225: 
226: ```toml
227: # .codex/agents/my-agent.toml — reasoning-heavy agent
228: model = "gpt-5.5"
229: 
230: # .codex/agents/my-codegen-agent.toml — code-focused agent
231: model = "gpt-5.5"
232: model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
233: ```
234: 
235: ---
236: 
237: ## 6. OUTPUT HANDLING
238: 
239: ### exec Mode Output
240: 
241: `codex exec` writes its output to stdout. Use shell redirection or command substitution to capture it.
242: 
243: ```bash
244: # Capture to file
245: codex exec "Generate a TypeScript interface for the User model" \
246:   --model gpt-5.5 > /tmp/user-interface.ts
247: 
248: # Capture to variable
249: RESULT=$(codex exec "List all exported functions in src/" --model gpt-5.5)
250: echo "$RESULT"
251: 
252: # Pipe to another command
253: codex exec "Generate SQL schema for users table" --model gpt-5.5 | psql -d mydb -f -
254: 
255: # Redirect stderr separately
256: codex exec "Analyze auth flow" --model gpt-5.5 > /tmp/analysis.txt 2>/tmp/errors.txt
257: ```
258: 
259: ### Requesting JSON Output
260: 
261: Codex provides native structured output. Use `--json` for the JSONL event stream and `--output-schema <FILE>` to validate the final response against a JSON Schema:
262: 
263: ```bash
264: # Emit JSONL events and validate the final response
265: codex exec --json --output-schema /tmp/analysis-schema.json \
266:   "Analyze src/auth.ts" --model gpt-5.5 > /tmp/analysis.jsonl
267: 
268: # Parse with jq
269: jq 'select(.type == "turn.completed")' /tmp/analysis.jsonl
270: ```
271: 
272: ### Exit Codes
273: 
274: | Code | Meaning |
275: |------|---------|
276: | `0` | Success |
277: | Non-zero | Error (check stderr for details) |
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## 7. INTERACTIVE COMMANDS
282: 
283: When running `codex` in interactive (full-screen TUI) mode, these slash commands are available:
284: 
285: | Command | Description |
286: |---------|-------------|
287: | `/review` | Review and approve/reject pending actions |
288: | `/model` | Display or switch the current model |
289: | `/help` | Show all available commands |
290: 
291: ### Inline Prompting
292: 
293: In the TUI, type your prompt directly and press Enter. Multi-line input is supported. Use Ctrl+C to cancel the current generation.
294: 
295: ### Session Operations in TUI
296: 
297: All session management is accessible from the TUI home screen when running `codex` without arguments:
298: 
299: - Select an existing session to resume it
300: - Start a new session from scratch
301: - Fork an existing session to branch it
302: 
303: ---
304: 
305: ## 8. SPECIAL INPUT SYNTAX
306: 
307: ### File References
308: 
309: Codex supports `@file` references to include file contents in the prompt context:
310: 
311: ```bash
312: # Single file
313: codex exec "@src/utils.ts Explain this file" --model gpt-5.5
314: 
315: # Multiple files
316: codex exec "@src/auth.ts @src/session.ts Find the circular dependency" \
317:   --model gpt-5.5
318: 
319: # In the TUI
320: # Type: @src/utils.ts refactor this to use the repository pattern
321: ```
322: 
323: ### Shell Integration
324: 
325: Use standard shell mechanisms to combine Codex with other tools:
326: 
327: ```bash
328: # Pass git diff as context
329: git diff HEAD~1 | codex exec "Summarize these changes" --model gpt-5.5
330: 
331: # Combine file content with prompt
332: cat src/auth.ts | codex exec "Add input validation to all functions" \
333:   --model gpt-5.5
334: 
335: # Pass error output for debugging
336: npm test 2>&1 | codex exec "Fix these failing tests" --sandbox workspace-write \
337:   --model gpt-5.5
338: ```
339: 
340: ### instructions.md Context File
341: 
342: Place an `instructions.md` in `.codex/` to inject persistent project context into every Codex session:
343: 
344: ```markdown
345: # Project Context
346: 
347: ## Architecture
348: - TypeScript monorepo with pnpm workspaces
349: - Express.js API with PostgreSQL (Prisma ORM)
350: - JWT authentication with refresh token rotation
351: 
352: ## Conventions
353: - Functional style; avoid classes except for Error types
354: - All public exports must have JSDoc
355: - Use Result<T, E> pattern for error handling
356: 
357: ## Do Not
358: - Modify prisma/schema.prisma without explicit instruction
359: - Add npm dependencies without justification
360: ```
361: 
362: ---
363: 
364: ## 9. CONFIGURATION FILES
365: 
366: ### Directory Structure
367: 
368: ```
369: CODEX_HOME/
370: ├── config.toml                 # Shared CLI defaults
371: ├── review.config.toml          # Named profile loaded by -p review
372: ├── context.config.toml         # Named profile loaded by -p context
373: ├── debug.config.toml           # Named profile loaded by -p debug
374: └── research.config.toml        # Named profile loaded by -p research
375: ```
376: 
377: ### config.toml Format
378: 
379: ```toml
380: # $CODEX_HOME/config.toml
381: model = "gpt-5.5"
382: model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
383: sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
384: ask_for_approval = "on-request"

386: 
387: ### Agent TOML Format
388: 
389: Each agent is a `.toml` file in `.codex/agents/`. Fields:
390: 
391: ```toml
392: # .codex/agents/example.toml
393: 
394: # Model configuration
395: model = "gpt-5.5"
396: model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
397: 
398: # Sandbox mode for this agent
399: sandbox_mode = "read-only"          # read-only | workspace-write | danger-full-access
400: 
401: # Agent instructions (developer-level system prompt)
402: developer_instructions = """
403: You are a specialized agent for [purpose].
404: [Detailed behavioral instructions here.]
405: """
406: ```
407: 
408: ### Invocation with Named Profile
409: 
410: ```bash
411: # Named profile via -p / --profile flag
412: codex exec -p review "Review src/auth.ts for security issues" --model gpt-5.5
413: 
414: # Git diff review via built-in subcommand
415: codex exec review "Focus on security issues" --commit HEAD --model gpt-5.5
416: codex review --uncommitted  # top-level shorthand
417: 
418: # Profile with sandbox override
419: codex exec -p debug "Fix the auth bug" -s workspace-write --model gpt-5.5
420: ```
421: 
422: ### Profile Configuration
423: 
424: Named profiles are layered TOML files in `CODEX_HOME`, loaded by the profile name. A `-p review` invocation reads `$CODEX_HOME/review.config.toml`; it does not read a `[profiles.review]` section from `config.toml`.
425: 
426: ```toml
427: # $CODEX_HOME/review.config.toml
428: sandbox_mode = "read-only"
429: model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
430: 
431: # $CODEX_HOME/debug.config.toml
432: sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
433: model_reasoning_effort = "xhigh"
434: ```
435: 
436: ```bash

438: codex exec -p review "Audit this codebase" --model gpt-5.5
439: ```
440: 
441: **Note:** The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define agent personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI feature (requires `multi_agent` feature flag). They are not loaded by the `-p` profile flag. Keep profile settings in the corresponding `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` file.
442: 
443: ---
444: 
445: ## 10. SANDBOX MODES
446: 
447: Sandbox modes control what Codex is permitted to do during execution. Always choose the least-permissive mode that allows the task to complete.
448: 
449: ### Mode Reference
450: 
451: | Mode | Flag Value | File Access | Shell Commands | Use Case |
452: |------|-----------|-------------|----------------|----------|
453: | **read-only** | `--sandbox read-only` | Read only | Restricted | Analysis, review, exploration, context mapping |
454: | **workspace-write** | `--sandbox workspace-write` | Read + write project files | Controlled | Code generation, refactoring, documentation |
455: | **danger-full-access** | `--sandbox danger-full-access` | Full filesystem | Unrestricted | System-level operations, migration scripts |
456: 
457: ### Safety Guidance
458: 
459: ```bash
460: # SAFE: Read-only for analysis
461: codex exec "Map the authentication flow" \
462:   --sandbox read-only --model gpt-5.5
463: 
464: # STANDARD: Workspace-write for code changes
465: codex exec "Add error handling to all API routes" \
466:   --sandbox workspace-write --model gpt-5.5
467: 
468: # ELEVATED RISK: Full access — use only when necessary and review all changes
469: codex exec "Migrate database schema and update all dependent files" \
470:   --sandbox danger-full-access --ask-for-approval untrusted --model gpt-5.5
471: ```
472: 
473: ### Mode Selection Heuristic
474: 
475: 1. **Read-only first:** Start with read-only for exploration and analysis tasks.
476: 2. **Workspace-write for generation:** Use when Codex must create or modify files in the project.
477: 3. **Full-access sparingly:** Reserve for tasks that genuinely require system-level access. Always pair with `--ask-for-approval untrusted`.
478: 
479: ---
480: 
481: ## 11. SESSION MANAGEMENT
482: 
483: ### Session Subcommands
484: 
485: | Subcommand | Description |
486: |------------|-------------|
487: | `codex` | Launch TUI; shows session picker on startup |
488: | `codex resume` | Resume a previous session interactively |
489: | `codex resume <session-id>` | Resume a specific session by ID |
490: | `codex fork` | Fork (branch) the current session to create a divergent copy |
491: | `codex fork <session-id>` | Fork a specific session by ID |
492: 
493: ### Session Picker
494: 
495: Running `codex` without arguments opens the full-screen TUI with a session picker. Select an existing session to resume it, or start a new session.
496: 
497: ### Scripted Session Resume
498: 
499: ```bash
500: # Resume a known session ID non-interactively
501: codex exec resume abc123 "Continue implementing the rate limiter" \
502:   --model gpt-5.5
503: 
504: # Fork a session before a risky operation
505: FORK_ID=$(codex fork abc123)
506: codex exec resume "$FORK_ID" "Attempt the migration" \
507:   --sandbox workspace-write --model gpt-5.5
508: ```
509: 
510: ### When to Use Each Operation
511: 
512: | Operation | When to Use |
513: |-----------|-------------|
514: | `resume` | Continue a multi-step task with existing context |
515: | `fork` | Try a different approach without losing the original session |
516: | New session | Fresh context; previous session is not relevant |
517: 
518: ---
519: 
520: ## 12. SUBCOMMANDS
521: 
522: | Subcommand | Description |
523: |------------|-------------|
524: | `codex exec` | Non-interactive execution; runs a single prompt and exits |
525: | `codex resume` | Resume a previous session |
526: | `codex fork` | Fork (branch) the current or a named session |
527: | `codex login` | Authenticate via ChatGPT OAuth (opens browser) |
528: | `codex logout` | Log out and clear stored OAuth credentials |
529: | `codex features` | Display available features and authentication status |
530: | `codex mcp` | Manage MCP (Model Context Protocol) server connections |
531: | `codex cloud` | Manage cloud operations such as `exec`, `status`, `list`, `apply`, and `diff`; use `codex login status` for shared authentication |
532: | `codex apply` | Apply a previously generated diff/patch |
533:

535: 
536: ## 13. TROUBLESHOOTING
537: 
538: | Problem | Cause | Solution |
539: |---------|-------|----------|
540: | `not authenticated` / `401 Unauthorized` | ChatGPT OAuth not configured | Run `codex login` (browser flow) |
541: | `Authentication failed` | OAuth session expired or invalid | Re-run `codex login` to re-authenticate |
542: | `OAuth not eligible` | Free-tier ChatGPT account | Upgrade to Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise |
543: | `Permission denied` on file | Sandbox mode too restrictive | Upgrade to `workspace-write` or `danger-full-access` as needed |
544: | `Command not found: codex` | Not installed or not in PATH | Run `npm i -g @openai/codex`; verify with `which codex` |
545: | Session resume fails | Session ID invalid or expired | List sessions via TUI; start a new session |
546: | Slow response | Large context or complex task | Break task into smaller steps; use `--sandbox read-only` for analysis |
547: | Unexpected file changes | Sandbox too permissive | Use `--ask-for-approval untrusted` with elevated sandbox modes |
548: | `--oss` model not responding | Ollama not running or no model loaded | Start Ollama: `ollama serve`; pull a model: `ollama pull codellama` |
549: | Web search not working | `--search` flag not specified | Add the top-level `--search` flag before `exec` (`codex --search exec …`) to enable live browsing |
550: | Windows compatibility | WSL not configured | Use WSL 2; native Windows support is experimental |
551: | Image not accepted | Unsupported format | Use PNG or JPEG only; convert other formats first |

16: # Codex CLI Built-in Tools Reference
17: 
18: Reference for all Codex CLI capabilities, highlighting unique features and Claude Code equivalents.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Core Principle
25: 
26: Delegate to Codex CLI for capabilities Claude Code lacks natively — especially `/review` for diff-aware code review workflows, `--search` for live web browsing, and session management (resume, fork) for multi-turn task continuity.
27: 
28: ### Purpose
29:

31: 
32: ### When to Use
33: 
34: - Choosing whether to delegate a task to Codex CLI or handle it in Claude Code
35: - Understanding which Codex flags and modes to use for different task types
36: - Mapping Claude Code capabilities to Codex CLI equivalents
37: - Leveraging Codex-exclusive features (/review workflow, --search, MCP, session management)
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. UNIQUE CAPABILITIES (NOT IN CLAUDE CODE)
42: 
43: These capabilities are exclusive to Codex CLI or provide significantly different workflows.
44: 
45: ### /review Command
46: 
47: **Built-in diff-aware code review.** The `/review` interactive command analyzes staged changes, recent commits, or branch differences using Codex's reasoning, producing structured review output.
48: 
49: **Capabilities:**
50: - Reviews staged git changes (diff-aware — only reviews what changed)
51: - Supports commit review: review a specific commit's changes
52: - Supports branch comparison: review all changes between two branches
53: - Produces categorized findings (bugs, security, style, performance)
54: - Interactive — runs inside the Codex TUI session
55: 
56: **Usage (Interactive TUI):**
57: 
58: ```bash
59: # Start interactive session
60: codex
61: 
62: # Inside TUI — review staged changes
63: /review
64: 
65: # Inside TUI — review a specific commit
66: /review HEAD~1
67: 
68: # Inside TUI — review branch diff
69: /review main..feature/auth
70: ```
71: 
72: **Best For:**
73: - Pre-commit review of staged changes
74: - Pull request preparation (branch comparison)
75: - Catching issues before pushing
76: - Generating review summaries for human reviewers
77: 
78: **Compared to Claude Code:** Claude Code performs code review by reading files directly. Codex's `/review` command is diff-aware — it focuses only on changed lines, reducing noise and improving relevance for incremental reviews.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: ### Web Search (--search)
83: 
84: **Live web browsing during task execution.** The `--search` flag enables Codex to browse the web during an `exec` session, retrieving current documentation, advisories, and community resources (pass it as a top-level flag before `exec`: `codex --search exec …`).
85: 
86: **Capabilities:**
87: - Searches the live web using OpenAI's browsing capability
88: - Returns current, ranked results with source citations
89: - Understands search intent and reformulates queries automatically
90: - Integrates web findings directly into code generation or analysis
91: - Supports follow-up searches within a single exec session
92: 
93: **Usage Examples:**
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # Research current library security advisories
97: codex --search exec "What are the latest security advisories for Express.js? Search the web." \
98:   --model gpt-5.5 --sandbox read-only
99: 
100: # Find migration guide
101: codex --search exec "Find the official Prisma 5 to 6 migration guide and summarize the breaking changes." \
102:   --model gpt-5.5 --sandbox read-only
103: 
104: # Compare packages with current data
105: codex --search exec "Compare zod vs yup for TypeScript validation as of 2026. Search for benchmarks." \
106:   --model gpt-5.5 --sandbox read-only
107: ```
108: 
109: **Output Format:**
110: - Inline citations with source URLs
111: - Summarized findings with links to originals
112: - Multiple sources cross-referenced when appropriate
113: 
114: **Best For:**
115: - Current documentation and API references
116: - Security advisories and CVE lookups
117: - Package discovery and comparison
118: - Checking latest versions and changelog entries
119: - Verifying claims against live sources
120: 
121: **Compared to Claude Code:** Claude Code has a WebSearch tool that provides search results. Codex's `--search` integrates web browsing directly into the reasoning loop, allowing Codex to use retrieved information immediately in code generation or analysis within the same session.
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ### MCP Server Integration (codex mcp)
126: 
127: **Model Context Protocol server support.** Codex CLI can connect to MCP servers, extending its capabilities with custom tools and data sources.
128: 
129: **Capabilities:**
130: - Connect to any MCP-compatible server
131: - Use MCP tools during `exec` sessions
132: - Configure MCP servers under `mcp_servers` in `.codex/config.toml` (or `~/.codex/config.toml`)
133: - Access custom data sources and APIs via MCP protocol
134: 
135: **Configuration:**
136: 
137: ```toml
138: # ~/.codex/config.toml: keep a real key out of the committed project .codex/config.toml
139: [mcp_servers.my-server]
140: command = "node"
141: args = ["./mcp-server.js"]
142: env = { MY_API_KEY = "<your key>" }
143: ```
144: 
145: **Usage:**
146: 
147: ```bash
148: # Start MCP management
149: codex mcp
150: 
151: # Use MCP tools in exec
152: codex exec "Use the database MCP tool to query user records" \
153:   --model gpt-5.5 --sandbox read-only
154: ```
155: 
156: **Best For:**
157: - Integrating custom data sources into Codex sessions
158: - Extending Codex with domain-specific tools
159: - Connecting to internal APIs or databases via MCP
160: 
161: **Compared to Claude Code:** Claude Code supports MCP natively, configured in the project `.mcp.json`. Codex CLI's MCP support follows the same protocol but is configured separately, under `mcp_servers` in `.codex/config.toml`.
162: 
163: ---
164: 
165: ### Session Management (resume, fork)
166: 
167: **Multi-turn workflow continuity.** Codex CLI supports resuming and forking sessions, enabling complex multi-step tasks that span multiple executions.
168: 
169: **Capabilities:**
170: - `codex resume [session-id]` — Continue a previous session with full context
171: - `codex fork [session-id]` — Branch from an existing session to explore alternatives
172: - Sessions persist tool call history and conversation context
173: - Useful for long-running tasks split across time
174: 
175: **Usage:**
176: 
177: ```bash
178: # List recent sessions
179: codex sessions list
180: 
181: # Resume the most recent session
182: codex resume
183: 
184: # Resume a specific session by ID
185: codex resume abc123
186: 
187: # Fork from a session to try an alternative approach
188: codex fork abc123
189: 
190: # Start exec and save session for later continuation
191: codex exec "Begin implementing the auth module. Stop after designing the interface." \
192:   --model gpt-5.5 --sandbox workspace-write
193: # Note the session ID from output, then later:
194: codex resume [session-id]
195: ```
196: 
197: **Best For:**
198: - Long implementation tasks split across multiple work sessions
199: - Exploring alternative implementation approaches (fork)
200: - Iterative refinement where prior context matters
201: - Multi-phase workflows where each phase builds on the last
202: 
203: **Compared to Claude Code:** Claude Code does not have built-in session persistence between invocations; it reconstructs continuity from the spec folder's `handover.md` and continuity docs. Codex's `resume`/`fork` maintains full conversation and tool-call context from the previous session.
204: 
205: ---
206: 
207: ### Image Input (--image / -i)
208: 
209: **Visual input for design-to-code and screenshot analysis.** Codex can accept image files as input, enabling workflows that start from visual artifacts.
210: 
211: **Capabilities:**
212: - Attach screenshots, mockups, diagrams, or design files
213: - Implement UI components directly from design images
214: - Analyze error screenshots or visual bugs
215: - Document visual outputs (charts, diagrams) via description
216: - Supports common image formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF)
217: 
218: **Usage:**
219: 
220: ```bash
221: # Implement a UI component from a design mockup
222: codex exec "Implement this React component to match the design." \
223:   --model gpt-5.5 -i ./designs/login-form.png --sandbox workspace-write
224: 
225: # Debug a visual error from a screenshot
226: codex exec "This screenshot shows a layout bug. Diagnose and fix @./src/components/Layout.tsx." \
227:   --model gpt-5.5 -i ./screenshots/layout-bug.png --sandbox workspace-write
228: 
229: # Multiple images
230: codex exec "Compare these two design versions and implement the better one." \
231:   --model gpt-5.5 -i design-v1.png -i design-v2.png --sandbox workspace-write
232: ```
233: 
234: **Best For:**
235: - Design-to-code workflows (Figma exports, mockups, wireframes)
236: - Visual bug reports (screenshot → root cause analysis)
237: - UI consistency audits (screenshot comparison)
238: - Diagram-to-implementation (architecture diagrams, ERDs)
239: 
240: **Compared to Claude Code:** Claude Code supports image reading via the `Read` tool (multimodal). Codex's `-i` flag passes images as direct session context, integrated into the exec workflow with sandbox controls.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ### Cloud Tasks (codex cloud)
245: 
246: **Cloud operations.** The `codex cloud` subcommand exposes the current cloud operation verbs. Authentication is shared with the local CLI and is checked with `codex login status`; do not look for a separate cloud-local auth flag.
247: 
248: **Capabilities:**
249: - `exec` — start a cloud execution
250: - `status` and `list` — inspect cloud work
251: - `apply` and `diff` — inspect or apply cloud-produced changes
252: 
253: **Usage:**
254: 
255: ```bash
256: # Check shared authentication before cloud operations
257: codex login status
258: 
259: # Inspect the live cloud operation surface
260: codex cloud --help
261: ```
262: 
263: **Best For:**
264: - Resource-intensive generation tasks
265: - Tasks where local environment setup is complex
266: - Offloading long-running work to remote execution
267: 
268: **Note:** Requires appropriate account permissions and may incur additional usage costs.
269: 
270: ---

280: | File reading | Read file contents | Automatic or `@./path/to/file.ts` |
281: | File writing | Create or overwrite a file | Automatic (requires `--sandbox workspace-write`) |
282: | Surgical edits | Replace text in a file | Automatic (targeted edits within files) |
283: | Multi-file read | Read multiple files | `@./file1.ts @./file2.ts` or `@./src/**/*.ts` |
284: | Directory listing | List files and directories | Automatic pattern exploration |
285: | File search | Find files by pattern | Automatic glob matching |
286: | Content search | Search for text/regex in files | Automatic code search |
287:

289:

292: | Command execution | Run shell commands | Requires `--sandbox workspace-write` or higher |
293: | Build and test | Run npm, cargo, pytest, etc. | Allowed at workspace-write and above |
294: | Git operations | git status, diff, add, commit | Allowed at workspace-write and above |
295: 
296: ### Interaction
297: 
298: | Capability | Description | Notes |
299: |------------|-------------|-------|
300: | Clarification | Ask for input when needed | Automatic within TUI sessions |
301: | Task tracking | Internal task management | Built into session context |
302:

305: ## 4. CLAUDE CODE VS. CODEX CLI CAPABILITY COMPARISON
306:

308: |------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------|
309: | **File reading** | `Read` | `read_file`, `@file` | Codex `@` syntax is concise |
310: | **File writing** | `Write`, `Edit` | Automatic write/edit | Codex requires `--sandbox workspace-write` |
311: | **Code search** | `Grep` (ripgrep) | Automatic content search | Claude's Grep is ripgrep-powered |
312: | **File discovery** | `Glob` | Automatic glob matching | Functionally equivalent |
313: | **Shell commands** | `Bash` | Automatic shell execution | Both require appropriate permissions |
314: | **Web fetch** | `WebFetch` | Automatic URL fetching | Similar capabilities |
315: | **Web search** | `WebSearch` | `--search` flag | Codex integrates browsing into reasoning loop |
316: | **Architecture analysis** | Manual (Grep+Read+Glob) | Agent-assisted analysis | Codex uses `@context` agent |
317: | **Memory/persistence** | External (Spec Kit spec folders) | Session resume/fork | Different approaches; Spec Kit is more structured |
318: | **Task tracking** | External (TodoWrite) | Internal session context | Codex tracks within session |
319: | **Browser automation** | External MCP | Not built-in | Both need external tools |
320: | **MCP integration** | Native + Code Mode | `.codex/config.toml` (`mcp_servers`) | Both support MCP protocol |
321: | **Multi-file read** | Multiple `Read` calls | `@glob` pattern | Codex batches natively |
322: | **Image analysis** | `Read` (multimodal) | `--image` / `-i` flag | Both support image input |
323: | **Code review (diff)** | Manual diff + Read | `/review` command | Codex `/review` is diff-aware |
324: | **Models** | 3 (Anthropic) | 1 (OpenAI: GPT-5.5) | Codex skill uses GPT-5.5 at configurable reasoning effort |

328: 
329: ---
330: 
331: ## 5. SANDBOX MODES
332: 
333: Codex CLI uses sandbox modes to control what actions are permitted during execution. Always select the most restrictive mode that allows the task to complete.
334: 
335: ### Mode Reference
336: 
337: | Mode | Flag | Permitted Actions | When to Use |
338: |------|------|-------------------|-------------|
339: | **Read-only** | `--sandbox read-only` | Read files, no writes, no shell commands | Review, audit, analysis, research |
340: | **Workspace-write** | `--sandbox workspace-write` | Read + write files in workspace, run build/test commands | Code generation, bug fixing, documentation |
341: | **Danger full access** | `--sandbox danger-full-access` | Full shell access including system operations | **Requires explicit user approval** |
342: 
343: ### Selection Guide
344: 
345: ```
346: What does the task need to do?
347:     │
348:     ├─► Read files only (review, analyze, explain)
349:     │   └─► --sandbox read-only
350:     │
351:     ├─► Write files within workspace (generate, fix, refactor)
352:     │   └─► --sandbox workspace-write
353:     │
354:     └─► System-level operations (install, configure OS)
355:         └─► --sandbox danger-full-access  ← ASK USER FIRST
356: ```
357: 
358: ### Approval Modes
359: 
360: | Mode | Flag | Behavior |
361: |------|------|----------|
362: | Prompt for untrusted | `--ask-for-approval untrusted` | Asks before potentially dangerous operations (default) |
363: | Prompt on request | `--ask-for-approval on-request` | Asks only when Codex explicitly requests approval |
364: | Never ask | `--ask-for-approval never` | Auto-approves all operations |
365: | Full auto | `--full-auto` | Low-friction mode — combine with caution |
366: 
367: ---

159: verification gates, and output contract.

172: 3. **Pure-mechanical command** with no agent semantics — the persona MAY be omitted, but the omission MUST be stated at the dispatch site.
173: 
174: Silence is never an exception.

177: 
178: ## 7. COMMON CLI PROMPT FAILURE PATTERNS
179: 
180: - Missing output format or success criteria
181: - Unbounded scope that lets the delegated CLI wander
182: - Vague verbs such as "improve", "look at", or "handle" without specifics
183: - No file, artifact, or interface anchors when repo context matters
184: - No guardrails for security, compliance, or "do not change" boundaries

199: ```
